title: Pearson Edexcel GCSE (9–1) History
subtitle: Option P5: Conflict in the Middle East, 1945–95

sections.title: Key Topic 1: The birth of the state of Israel, 1945–63

topics.title: The British Withdrawal and the Creation of Israel
points: **Conflicting interests and demands** of Jews and Arabs within the British Mandate.
**Key events leading to the end of the British Mandate**, partition and the creation of Israel, including the **significance of the bombing of the King David Hotel** and **UN Resolution 181**.
**Key events of the Arab-Israeli war (1948–49)**.
topics.narrative_blurb: Post-war violence exposed the **conflicting interests and demands of Jews and Arabs within the British Mandate**. The Irgun's **bombing of the King David Hotel** hastened Britain’s departure, prompting **UN Resolution 181** for **partition and the creation of Israel**. As the **end of the British Mandate** arrived in May 1948, five Arab armies invaded, launching the **key events of the Arab-Israeli war (1948–49)**.

topics.title: Aftermath of the 1948–49 War
points: **Territorial changes** and their impact.
The **refugee status of Palestinian Arabs**.
The creation of the **Israeli Defence Forces** and the **Law of Return**.
**US aid to Israel**.
Israel’s **relations with Egypt**.
topics.narrative_blurb: The 1949 armistices brought sweeping **territorial changes and their impact**, entrenching the permanent **refugee status of Palestinian Arabs**. Israel ensured survival through **the creation of the Israeli Defence Forces** and the 1950 **Law of Return** for Jewish immigrants, bolstered by vital **US aid to Israel**, while border friction and blockades poisoned **Israel’s relations with Egypt**.

topics.title: Increased Tension, 1955–63
points: **Nasser** and Egypt’s **leadership of the Arab world**.
The events and significance of **Israeli attacks on Gaza in 1955** and **Sinai in 1956**.
The events and significance of the **Suez Crisis (1956)**, including the **formation of the UAR in 1958**.
topics.narrative_blurb: Gamal Abdel Nasser secured **Nasser and Egypt’s leadership of the Arab world** through anti-Western defiance. Escalating skirmishes, including the **Israeli attacks on Gaza in 1955** and **Sinai in 1956**, culminated in the **events and significance of the Suez Crisis (1956)**. Despite military retreat, Nasser triumphed politically, cementing prestige in the **formation of the UAR in 1958**.

topics.title: The Six Day War, 1967
points: The significance of the **Cairo Conference (1964)**. **Escalating tension between Israel, Syria and Jordan**: **Syria’s support for Fatah**, **Israel’s raid on Samu** and **events of 7 April 1967**.
The **actions of the USSR, Nasser and the USA in the period leading to war**.
**Key events of the war**.
topics.narrative_blurb: Arab summits underscored **the significance of the Cairo Conference (1964)**. **Escalating tension between Israel, Syria and Jordan** flared through **Syria’s support for Fatah**, **Israel’s raid on Samu**, and dogfights in the **events of 7 April 1967**. Driven by **the actions of the USSR, Nasser and the USA in the period leading to war**, Israel struck pre-emptively on 5 June, dominating the **key events of the war** in six days.

topics.title: Aftermath of the 1967 War
points: **UN Resolution 242** and **continued dispute over the Suez Canal**.
**Palestinian refugees and the significance of the occupied territories: Golan Heights, Gaza Strip, West Bank, Sinai and East Jerusalem**.

The **use of terrorism, Israel’s response and international attitudes towards the Palestine issue**: the **PFLP airplane hijacks of 1970**; **Black September and the Munich Olympics**. The **expulsion of the PLO from Jordan (1970)**.
topics.narrative_blurb: Conquest generated new **Palestinian refugees and the significance of the occupied territories: Golan Heights, Gaza Strip, West Bank, Sinai and East Jerusalem**. **UN Resolution 242** failed to resolve the **continued dispute over the Suez Canal**. In response, guerrilla factions escalated **the use of terrorism, Israel’s response and international attitudes towards the Palestine issue**, including the **PFLP airplane hijacks of 1970**, the **expulsion of the PLO from Jordan (1970)**, and **Black September and the Munich Olympics**.

topics.title: Israel and Egypt, 1967–73
points: **Egyptian relations with Israel, the USA, the USSR and other Arab states**.
Israel’s **consolidation of control of the occupied territories**.
**Key events of the Yom Kippur War (1973) and its aftermath**.
topics.narrative_blurb: President Sadat reshaped **Egyptian relations with Israel, the USA, the USSR and other Arab states**, preparing to challenge **Israel’s consolidation of control of the occupied territories**. On 6 October 1973, Arab armies launched a surprise assault on the Bar-Lev Line, sparking the **key events of the Yom Kippur War (1973) and its aftermath**, ending Israeli invulnerability.

sections.title: Key Topic 3: Attempts at a solution, 1974–95

topics.title: Diplomatic Negotiations
points: The **significance of the oil crisis and the involvement of the USA and the USSR**.
**Kissinger**, **‘shuttle diplomacy’** and the **reopening of the Suez Canal**.
**Sadat’s visit to Israel (1977)**, **Begin’s visit to Egypt (1977)**, **US President Carter and Camp David (1978)** and the **Treaty of Washington (1979)**.
topics.narrative_blurb: Global fallout highlighted **the significance of the oil crisis and the involvement of the USA and the USSR**. Henry **Kissinger** pursued **‘shuttle diplomacy’** enabling **the reopening of the Suez Canal**. Bilateral diplomacy flourished through **Sadat’s visit to Israel (1977)** and **Begin’s visit to Egypt (1977)**, mediated by **US President Carter and Camp David (1978)** to achieve the historic **Treaty of Washington (1979)**.

topics.title: The Palestinian Issue
points: **Arafat’s speech to the UN (1974)**. The **significance of PLO activities in Lebanon**.
**Israeli reprisals, the invasion of Lebanon (1982) and the results**.
The **Israeli occupied territories and the First Palestinian Intifada (1987–93)**.
topics.narrative_blurb: Global attention surged after **Arafat’s speech to the UN (1974)**. However, **the significance of PLO activities in Lebanon** provoked sharp **Israeli reprisals, the invasion of Lebanon (1982) and the results**, forcing guerrilla evacuation. Frustration within the **Israeli occupied territories** eventually exploded in December 1987 into the stone-throwing civil disobedience of the **First Palestinian Intifada (1987–93)**.

topics.title: Attempts at a Solution
points: The **significance of Arafat’s renunciation of terrorism in a speech at the UN (1988)**.
**Changing superpower policies in the Middle East: US involvement in the Gulf War (1991), and the end of the Cold War**.
**Arafat, Rabin and the Oslo Accords (1993)**; the **setting up of the Palestinian National Authority**; **Israel-Jordan peace treaty (1994)**; **Oslo II (1995)**.
topics.narrative_blurb: Diplomatic momentum accelerated following **the significance of Arafat’s renunciation of terrorism in a speech at the UN (1988)**. Spurred by **changing superpower policies in the Middle East: US involvement in the Gulf War (1991), and the end of the Cold War**, historic negotiations produced **Arafat, Rabin and the Oslo Accords (1993)**, the **setting up of the Palestinian National Authority**, the **Israel-Jordan peace treaty (1994)**, and **Oslo II (1995)**.
